summary: Developer threat model for a local content forge that protects provider credentials, remote join secrets and approvals, filesystem state, trusted UI authority, and machine availability from hostile files and explicitly approved remote clients. The layers document canonical parse-not-execute conversion with semantic Round-Trip guarantees, bounded archives, pre-compile ReDoS rejection plus runtime budgets, sanitized rendering and CSP, capability-starved Lua with worker termination and value-only messages, a three-asset sandbox origin whose packaged proof is blocked, the primary loopback API plus separately gated remote listeners, and Kit's encrypted BYOK vault. Honest gaps include packaged-host sandbox measurement, malformed-vault recovery, the absent non-Windows passphrase flow, and provider redirects that are not revalidated after the initial host check. Each layer names its enforcement and test boundary so scaffolded behavior is not presented as packaged proof.

sections.title: Threat model
sections.summary: Protected assets are provider credentials and connection secrets, remote join secrets and device approvals, host-only controls, the local filesystem and user-owned studio folder, the trusted UI origin and per-launch bearer, and machine availability. The adversary includes untrusted imported content and, when Remote access is explicitly enabled, approved remote clients and the remote listener. The primary server remains a loopback forge. Trust ends at every file and request, so input is parsed once, capabilities are absent unless deliberately supplied, and gates fail closed. Named soft edges at this boundary are unmeasured packaged-host origin separation plus Kit vault recovery and non-Windows setup; provider redirect limits remain documented with the provider egress layer.

sections.title: The layers
sections.summary: The layers combine structural prevention with bounded execution and explicitly scoped evidence. 1. Parse, not execute keeps private payloads opaque and conversion canonical. 2. Decompression caps on archives bound selection and inflation. 3. ReDoS-guarded regex rejects dangerous AST shapes before native execution. 4. Sanitized rendering applies DOMPurify, pure policy, and CSP. 5. The Lua sandbox and its resource budgets remove host capabilities, cap state, and kill workers. 6. Distinct-origin sandbox isolation adds a second HTTP-tested listener whose packaged proof remains blocked. 7. The token-gated primary local server and separately enabled remote listeners protect API authority with request gates, join secrets, device approval, and host-only controls. 8. The BYOK provider vault encrypts configurations while documenting passphrase, redirect, and recovery limits.

children.title: 1. Parse, not execute
children.summary: Every format enters and leaves through the canonical superset rather than converting directly to another platform. Source-specific scripts, extension blocks, and layout remain opaque escrow data. Cross-format exports carry only canonical content, preventing one application's executable payload from being copied into another, while typed adapter contracts prevent cross-kind writers. The engine and server do not evaluate imported scripts; the user-invoked Lua Test Bench is the sole execution exception. Same-format Round-Trip requires semantic preservation unless a format specification explicitly declares and fixtures prove a byte-level tier.

children.title: 2. Decompression caps on archives
children.summary: unzipBounded handles untrusted charx, byaf, Lumiverse, and sprite archives with checks before and after inflation. It limits total entries, selected compressed and declared sizes, per-entry output, and aggregate output; missing originalSize remains bounded by compressed size and actual post-inflate length. Card containers allow 96 MiB archives, 512 entries, 64 MiB per selected entry, and 96 MiB selected total, while packs use tighter 48 MiB and 256-entry ceilings. Violations throw ArchiveLimitError and required entries are never silently omitted.

children.title: 3. ReDoS-guarded regex
children.summary: Because one synchronous native RegExp call cannot be interrupted, validateRule is the primary defense: it rejects excessive complexity and dangerous structures such as nested unbounded quantifiers, star-overlapping alternation, and quantified backreferences before compilation. Runtime execution adds per-rule and set budgets plus a 1,000-match ceiling, but its timeout observes only between native calls and cannot rescue a pathological match already running. The editor's structural ReDoS lens is advisory rather than authoritative. Validation, application, and AST warning behavior have separate suites.

children.title: 4. Sanitized rendering
children.summary: Stored markup passes through marked and then DOMPurify as the final transformation before innerHTML. Active, form, embedding, style, media-fetching, and script tags are forbidden; data attributes and surviving fetch attributes are removed, and links receive scheme, target, and rel hardening. A DOM-free policy independently enforces a 200k input limit, http/https/mailto links, constrained inline-style properties, and rejection of url, var, import, and expression indirection. Sealed previews and portrait responses add restrictive CSP, sandbox, and nosniff headers. Pure policy and DOM rendering tests cover separate halves.

children.title: 5. The Lua sandbox and its resource budgets
children.summary: Lua executes only when the user invokes the Risu Test Bench. Wasmoon opens a deliberately small pure-library set, excludes io, os, debug, and package, then removes loaders and host-reaching globals. Typed ceilings cover wall time, heap, source, wire data, and host state; release maxima include five seconds, 64 MiB heap, and 2 MiB source and state budgets, and callers cannot raise them. Each run occurs in a Worker that is terminated at deadline. Its versioned value-only protocol accepts plain data, rejects functions, exotic prototypes, forbidden keys, and secret-shaped fields, and never receives the API bearer.

children.title: 6. Distinct-origin sandbox isolation (packaged-host proof BLOCKED)
children.summary: ADR-009 places sandbox assets on a second ephemeral loopback listener that serves only the Lua worker, regex worker, and glue.wasm, with no API, index, studio paths, or session token. This adds an origin boundary beyond a killable same-origin Worker. Bun tests prove the HTTP allowlist, CORS, protocol rejection, and token absence, but do not measure how packaged WebView2 treats the two authorities, storage, crossOriginIsolated, or credentialed API access. Plan 017 therefore remains blocked for full proof. Bind failure falls back to a degraded same-origin worker and must not be called isolated.

children.title: 7. Token-gated local server and opt-in remote access
children.summary: The primary Studio listener binds 127.0.0.1 and creates a random per-launch bearer. API requests receive Host validation against DNS rebinding; mutations require an allowed Origin and constant-time token comparison, while GET and HEAD use Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site refusal because browser subresource reads cannot attach the bearer. Missing mutation Origin fails closed. Streaming readers cap inspect bodies at 64 MiB and JSON at 32 MiB with 413 on overflow. Remote tunnel and LAN modes are separate, explicitly enabled boundaries with join secrets, device approval, and host-only control routes documented in the remote-access threat model.

children.title: 8. BYOK provider vault (shipping in Kit)
children.summary: Kit encrypts the complete provider configuration list, credentials included, into one vault file and holds plaintext only after opening it in process. Saves seal a private temporary file and atomically replace the previous document. Windows uses DPAPI. A portable passphrase backend exists and sealed blobs retain backend identity, but current settings do not collect or supply the passphrase, leaving non-Windows first-run setup incomplete. Provider egress normalizes the endpoint and validates the initial request host, but runtime redirects are not revalidated. Credentials stay out of messages, tools, content, exports, transcripts, and privacy receipts. Malformed outer-file recovery is also incomplete, and Kit remains source-preview only.

sections.title: Status at a glance
sections.summary: The generated status figure condenses the preceding defense layers into a scan of what is enforced, what has automated code-layer evidence, what remains scaffolded, and what is blocked on packaged-host measurement. It is a navigation aid rather than a substitute for each layer's caveats and source references.

sections.title: What this document does not claim
sections.summary: The document does not call the Lua environment fully isolated because its second-origin behavior is proven at the Bun HTTP layer, not inside packaged WebView2. It does not claim exploitation is impossible; controls reduce blast radius as defense in depth. Regex time budgets cannot interrupt one catastrophic native call, so structural rejection remains essential. Kit's vault lacks complete malformed-envelope recovery and a settings-driven portable passphrase flow, Kit is absent from current release binaries, and provider redirects are not revalidated after the initial host check. A same-origin sandbox fallback is explicitly degraded and receives no isolation claim.
